pattern: union two differently-headered tables, pivot, compute a difference, rank
question: which centre saw the biggest fall in attendance rate from 2023 to 2024
gold_sql: WITH combined AS (SELECT "Centre" AS centre, 2023 AS year, "Avg Daily Present" / "Enrolled Kids" * 100.0 AS rate FROM attendance_2023 UNION ALL SELECT centre_name AS centre, 2024 AS year, average_attendance / enrolment * 100.0 AS rate FROM attendance_2024) , by_year AS (SELECT centre, AVG(CASE WHEN year = 2023 THEN rate END) AS avg_2023, AVG(CASE WHEN year = 2024 THEN rate END) AS avg_2024 FROM combined GROUP BY centre) SELECT centre, avg_2023 - avg_2024 AS drop_pp FROM by_year ORDER BY drop_pp DESC, centre LIMIT 1
sql_duckdb: WITH centre_attendance_2023 AS (SELECT "Centre", "Month", "Enrolled Kids", "Avg Daily Present" FROM "attendance_2023"), centre_attendance_2024 AS (SELECT "centre_name" AS "Centre", "month" AS "Month", "enrolment" AS "Enrolled Kids", "average_attendance" AS "Avg Daily Present" FROM "attendance_2024"), centre_attendance_change AS (SELECT ca2023."Centre", ca2023."Month", ca2023."Enrolled Kids", ca2023."Avg Daily Present", ca2024."Avg Daily Present" AS "2024 Avg Daily Present", (ca2024."Avg Daily Present" - ca2023."Avg Daily Present") / NULLIF(NULLIF(ca2023."Avg Daily Present", 0), 0) AS "Attendance Rate Change" FROM centre_attendance_2023 AS ca2023 JOIN centre_attendance_2024 AS ca2024 ON ca2023."Centre" = ca2024."Centre" AND ca2023."Month" = ca2024."Month") SELECT "Centre", "Month", "Enrolled Kids", "Avg Daily Present", "2024 Avg Daily Present", "Attendance Rate Change" FROM centre_attendance_change WHERE "Attendance Rate Change" = (SELECT MAX("Attendance Rate Change") FROM centre_attendance_change)

attempts.prompt:
You translate ordinary questions into exactly one read-only DuckDB SELECT or WITH query.

Return SQL only. Never write files, install software, calculate values yourself, or invent columns.

Use only the supplied schema. Preserve relevant scope from earlier turns unless the newest question changes it.

A requested rate must use its stated numerator and denominator. Percentage-point change means later percentage minus earlier percentage, not relative growth.

When the user explicitly asks for percent or percentage, multiply numerator divided by denominator by 100.

When the user asks to compare years or groups without asking for a change, keep those year/group columns and requested measures in the output.

When several known category values are named, filter them separately with IN rather than concatenating them.

Use NULLIF for denominators. Missing values remain missing and are not zero.

CREATE TABLE "attendance_2023" (
  "Centre" VARCHAR,
  "Month" VARCHAR,
  "Enrolled Kids" BIGINT,
  "Avg Daily Present" BIGINT
);

  "centre_name" VARCHAR,
  "month" VARCHAR,
  "enrolment" BIGINT,

);

which centre saw the biggest fall in attendance rate from 2023 to 2024

WITH 
  centre_attendance_2023 AS (
    SELECT 
      "Centre", 
      "Month", 
      "Enrolled Kids", 
      "Avg Daily Present" 
    FROM 
      "attendance_2023"
  ),
  centre_attendance_2024 AS (
    SELECT 
      "centre_name" AS "Centre", 
      "month" AS "Month", 
      "enrolment" AS "Enrolled Kids", 
      "average_attendance" AS "Avg Daily Present" 
    FROM 
      "attendance_2024"
  ),
  centre_attendance_change AS (
    SELECT 
      ca2023."Centre", 
      ca2023."Month", 
      ca2023."Enrolled Kids", 
      ca2023."Avg Daily Present", 
      ca2024."Avg Daily Present" AS "2024 Avg Daily Present", 
      (ca2024."Avg Daily Present" - ca2023."Avg Daily Present") / NULLIF(ca2023."Avg Daily Present", 0) AS "Attendance Rate Change"
    FROM 
      centre_attendance_2023 ca2023
    JOIN 
      centre_attendance_2024 ca2024 ON ca2023."Centre" = ca2024."Centre" AND ca2023."Month" = ca2024."Month"
  )
SELECT 
  "Centre", 
  "Month", 
  "Enrolled Kids", 
  "Avg Daily Present", 
  "2024 Avg Daily Present", 
  "Attendance Rate Change"
FROM 
  centre_attendance_change
WHERE 
  "Attendance Rate Change" = (SELECT MAX("Attendance Rate Change") FROM centre_attendance_change)
